source: Regrouped from the project's DWSIM 10.2.3 characterisation of Tia Juana Light (tjl-ledezma2019-dwsim1023-13pc-r1) from the TBP data in Ledezma-Martinez, Design of Crude Oil Distillation Systems with Preflash Units, PhD thesis, University of Manchester (2019), taken from Watkins (1979) via Chen (2008) by constrained mass-CDF reconstruction; DWSIM 10.2.5.0 Riazi-Daubert Tc/Pc; PR78 saturation-fitted omega; mass-conserved caloric interpolation. Estimated heavy extrapolation.

fluid_domain.evidence: Fluid network only (not the column range): the 298.15..900 K caloric fit continued to 293.15 K (the bundled ambient continuation qualified in the fluid-network batch, with the pure-component viscosity tables sampled from 293.15 K); 100 Pa..2 MPa is the span the network evaluates this record over (PR78 with every phase at its own pressure since P3 WP4; above 2 MPa this record is not qualified).

freezing.source: Estimated upper bound: the melting point of the n-paraffin of the fraction's molar mass 678.3954100855394 g/mol (icheme:crude_pc10, revision crude-regrouped-r1), Riazi and Al-Sahhaf, Ind. Eng. Chem. Res. 34 (1995) 4145, Tm = 397 - exp(6.5096 - 0.14187 M^0.47), fitted for C5..C40 (M about 70..565); this M lies beyond C40, so the value is extrapolated. A fraction freezes over a range (cloud and pour points lie lower). Data only: never a validity floor or a range end.

thermochemistry.source: Estimated. Formula CHx: hydrogen 11.41854878234998 wt% from Cragoe 1929 (US Bureau of Standards Miscellaneous Publication 97, Thermal Properties of Petroleum Products), 26 - 15 SG, at the molar mass 678.3954100855394 g/mol of icheme:crude_pc10 (revision crude-regrouped-r1), the rest carbon; SG 0.9720967478433347 = its standard liquid density over 999.016 kg/m3, water at 60 F; sulfur ignored (owner decision E23). Formation enthalpy back-computed so that Hess's law to CO2 and H2O (gas), on ChemSep v8.3's ideal-gas heats of formation (-393510 and -241814 J/mol), gives Cragoe's net heat 51.916 - 8.792 SG^2 - 0.2122 H = 41.1847893580079 MJ/kg. Against 177 ChemSep C5+ hydrocarbons that heat has -0.3 % bias and 0.5 % mean absolute error for paraffins and naphthenes, +2.5 % and 2.8 % for aromatics (COMBUSTION_FLAMMABILITY_REVIEW.md, batch 2026-11-04-open-thermo-data). Cragoe 1929 is a US Government work. Computed by tools/crude-grades/thermochemistry.mjs. Data only.

flammability.source: Estimated, Burgess-Wheeler: LFL x LHV = 4319 vol% kJ/mol, the median over the 22 hydrocarbons of the world list (0.2 % bias, 7.5 % mean absolute error, 23 % largest; COMBUSTION_FLAMMABILITY_REVIEW.md), on the Hess heat of this record's estimated thermochemistry. Constant with temperature (owner decision E23). No upper limit: no correlation is good enough (Jones, 25 % mean absolute error).

combustion.source: Hess's law on this record's thermochemistry (cragoe-1929-chx-r1): the formula burnt to CO2, H2O (gas), SO2 and N2 on the ideal-gas heats of formation at 298.15 K of icheme:chemsep_carbon_dioxide (chemsep-8.3-hf-r1), icheme:water (chemsep-8.3-hf-r1) and icheme:chemsep_sulfur_dioxide (chemsep-8.3-hf-r1). Computed by tools/heating-values/heating-values.mjs. Read by a fired heater's burners.

liquid.source: Twu, Ind. Eng. Chem. Process Des. Dev. 24 (1985) 1287: kinematic viscosity at 100 F and 210 F from this record's normal boiling point and standard density (n-alkane reference plus specific-gravity correction), continued in temperature by the ASTM D341 two-point (Walther) form; dynamic viscosity = kinematic x Rackett saturated-liquid density (Spencer-Danner, Yamada-Gunn Z_RA from this record's acentric factor) anchored at the standard density, held at its critical value above Tc; capped at 1e12 Pa s. Correlation estimate, no measured data; extrapolated beyond the correlation's fitted range for SG >= 1.0 (crude_pc11, crude_pc12). Generated by tools/crude-grades/cut-tables.mjs.

vapor.source: DWSIM 10.2.5.0 AUX_VAPVISCi with reconstructed MW, SG, NBP, Tc, Pc and PR78 omega; estimated vapor continuation
